words.plain: The Sea of Galilee [Greek: the word fresh here describes these bodies of water] is quite large for the Middle East — about 13 miles from north to south, and 7½ miles east to west at its widest. The Jordan River flows through it, entering in the north and exiting in the south. It was the working center of the local fishing economy.

words.meaning: Imperfect passive singular The nets were actually tearing in two (dia-) and so they would lose all the fish.
words.plain: Were breaking [Greek: dierrsseto — the nets were actually tearing in two]. If the nets gave way, the catch would be lost entirely. The miracle immediately threatened to undo itself — which is why they called for help so urgently. Even the blessing required fast action.

words.meaning: Imperfect tense. The fame of Jesus kept going.
words.plain: Went abroad [Greek: diercheto — 'kept going,' imperfect tense]. The fame of Jesus spread continuously, moving out in all directions without stopping. The more Jesus told people to keep quiet, the more they talked. His reputation was traveling faster than he was.

words.meaning: Imperfect tense again. The more the report spread, the more the crowds came
words.plain: Came together [Greek: synrchonto — 'kept coming,' imperfect tense again]. The crowds kept arriving — not a single gathering but a steady, growing flow. As the news spread outward, it pulled people inward toward wherever Jesus was.
